subject: Finalizing latency commitments for Hosted API - p50/p95 measurement approach

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The procurement team asked me to get a short, written proposal for the latency commitments we discussed so we can circulate internally. Specifically they want: p50/p95 numeric targets, how you measure them (windowing and aggregation), and what carveouts (maintenance / holidays / regional failovers) look like.

A few quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether p95 is measured at request-level or as a rolling percentile over a window?
- What measurement window do you propose for enterprise SLAs — daily, 24hr rolling, 7-day?
- We need an initial set of evidence files (benchmarks) to attach to the redlines packet.

Were targeting a go/no-go from Procurement by end of week. Can you share a concrete proposal we can feed into legal and finance?

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — draft numbers and questions

Samantha,

Appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise proposal you can share with Procurement and Legal. Ive attached the benchmark CSV and our evidence playbook (see files). If you want I can also export a trimmed report for your vendor packet.

Proposal (high level):
- Targets: p50 = 60 ms, p95 = 420 ms for the hosted API (production traffic shape similar to your demo traces).
- Measurement approach: p50 computed per calendar day as the median of all successful request latencies; p95 computed as a 24-hour rolling percentile evaluated hourly with a 7-day enforcement window for SLA crediting.
  - Explanation: p95 rolling evaluation reduces sensitivity to short-lived bursts while preserving responsiveness to sustained regressions.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (pre-announced up to 4 hours), emergency regional maintenance (up to 6 hours), and brief outage protectors for cross-regional failovers (automatic fallback for up to 3 hours).
- Exceptions: we propose a temporary leniency for seasonal peak events (up to 3 days per calendar quarter) with prior notice and agreed mitigation plan.
- Remedies: standard SLA credits on a sliding scale if the 7-day enforcement window shows sustained breach; single-day transient spikes do not automatically trigger credits.

Operational notes for your engineers (short):
- We measure latency at the ingress layer post-authentication and pre-streaming to ensure consistent boundaries across payloads.
- Time synchronization: all timestamps are UTC; sampling is disabled for SLA measurement (we include all successful requests).
- Regional fallback: where appropriate we maintain separate regional baselines and apply cross-region smoothing when failovers occur (diagram attached).

Attachments: latency-bench-finbridge-20280810.csv, slo-evidence-playbook.pdf, redwood-regional-fallback-diagram.png

If that reads OK, Laura and I can convert this into contract language for the MSA. Happy to tighten p95 if you can share a 48-hour high-burst sample — we can run a targeted bench.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Team, quick technical addendum for Procurements engineers:

- The p50/p95 numbers Vanessa proposed assume requests with typical payload sizes (prompt + system tokens) similar to the traces Finbridge shared — 512 token context and responses averaging 60 tokens. For very long contexts or streaming-heavy patterns p95 can widen; we can quantify that.
- Measurement windows detail: our pipeline computes per-request latency (milliseconds) and maintains a sliding hourly histogram. The 24-hour rolling percentile is computed from the union of hourly histograms; we then apply a 7-day rolling enforcement that requires 5 of the last 7 daily checks to be within the committed threshold before crediting is withheld. This prevents isolated infra incidents from immediately triggering credits.
- Burst carveouts: we recommend a daylight burst carveout (4-hour reserve) for planned marketing events. For unplanned emergencies we maintain a short grace period while we engage on mitigation.

If Finbridge is asking for stricter p95 figures in the contract well need to either: (a) reserve more capacity under a dedicated pool, or (b) accept narrower windows for measurement (e.g., 24-hour strict enforcement) and price accordingly. I can produce a short cost delta table if that helps.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Serving Runtime

2) Finance wants to understand the cost to tighten p95 to 320 ms. Karthik, the dedicated pool option sounds reasonable; please send a delta estimate (capacity + premium) we can budget against.

We attached a short burst sample from last quarter (finbridge-burst-sample-0728.json) to illustrate violation modes — curious whether that would shift your measurement choice.

Wed like to get to an internal decision by end of day Friday (24 Aug).

Best,
Samantha

Samantha — looping in a brief suggested clause you can drop into the MSA redline pack. This is intentionally tight and contract-ready; we can reword to match your lawyers style.

Suggested MSA snippet (plain text):
"Latency Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will maintain the Hosted API latency commitments of p50 ≤ 60 ms and p95 ≤ 420 ms as measured using Redwoods standardized telemetry. p50 will be calculated per calendar day as the median of all successful requests. p95 will be evaluated via a 24-hour rolling percentile with enforcement applied across a 7-day rolling window. Scheduled maintenance events (notified ≥ 72 hours in advance, up to 4 hours) and up to three ad-hoc seasonal peak carveouts per calendar quarter will be exempt from credit calculations. In the event of a sustained breach (5 of 7 days in the 7-day enforcement window exceed the committed threshold), Cliente is eligible for SLA credits as set forth in Schedule X."

If Procurement wants the 320 ms number we can produce a parallel clause and a one-line premium. Karthik — can you add the delta pricing and expected reserved capacity for 320 ms p95?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
